title: Alternative approach for .NET WASM: Bypassing NativeAOT trimming via Memory-Mapped synchronization
body:
> Proposal: "Magnet Bridge" framework for .NET Web Export
> I’ve been following the discussions and current PRs. It seems we are hitting a wall with hard-linking and NativeAOT trimming. I’d like to propose an alternative architectural direction I call the "Magnet Bridge".
> 
> Instead of trying to force Godot APIs into a worker or struggling with static linking, we should treat the communication as a Shared Data Field.
> 
> How it works:
> 
> Decoupled Runtimes: Use a SharedArrayBuffer as the only bridge between .NET and Godot C++.
> 
> C# (Data Provider): The C# side only writes raw game state (transforms, health, etc.) to fixed memory offsets. Because it doesn't call any Engine APIs, it is 100% safe from NativeAOT trimming and won't break when .NET internals change.
> 
> Engine (Data Consumer): Godot C++ acts like a "Magnet". During the process loop, it simply pulls (polls) the raw data from those memory addresses to update the scene.
> 
> Why this helps:
> 
> 1.GDExtension Support: It doesn’t mess with -sMAIN_MODULE, so we don't lose GDExtension compatibility like the current static lib approach.
> 2.Performance: No object marshaling overhead. With Atomic barriers and Double-buffering, we can sync thousands of entities with sub-1ms latency.
> 3.Future-proof: It’s version-agnostic. .NET 10 or 11 won't break it because we are talking via memory, not fragile bindings.
> **I'm sharing this as a conceptual framework for the community to explore. I believe this decoupled approach is the cleanest way to get C# back on the web without the usual "noisy" hacks.** 

 _Originally posted by @thanik123789-coder in [#70796](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/70796#issuecomment-4406173210)_
